shows that TEPs following stimulation of the rsFC-derived
hotspot were similar to those evoked by the MEP-derived hotspot
(group-averaged butterfly plots and TEPs topographies). The stimula
tion of the motor hotspots elicited high-amplitude lateralized EEG re
sponses. Well-described peaks following M1 stimulation (including P30,
P60 and N100) were clearly identifiable across conditions. Signal to
pographies across time were localized to the motor system and were
highly similar between the two conditions. As expected, MEPs elicited
from the rsFC-derived hotspot were slightly smaller and less consistent
than those from the MEP-defined site.
Similarities were tested across several neurophysiological measures.
